company.name: Amwaste LLC
company.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling
company.description: Amwaste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling services in the Southeastern United States. Its customer base includes residential, commercial, construction and industrial end markets across Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana. The business operates an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by owned disposal sites, transfer stations, and recycling infrastructure. Public materials describe a platform with more than 300,000 customers, eight landfill sites, ten transfer stations, and a materials recovery facility. The company has expanded through bolt-on acquisitions and local contract wins to deepen density in its core Southeastern markets. 3i invested growth capital through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in July 2023, and current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

Acquired the Sylvan Springs Waste Complex from Meredith Environmental.
Acquired the Whitestone Valley C&D Landfill and four transfer stations from Cash Environmental Resources.
3i North American Infrastructure Fund completed its growth-capital investment in Amwaste.
Acquired Waste Away Environmental in Milledgeville, Georgia.

company.name: EC Waste
company.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, and landfill services
company.description: EC Waste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, and disposal services across Puerto Rico. Its customers include residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal accounts served through an island-wide operating footprint. The business uses an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by disposal sites, transfer infrastructure, hauling operations, and related environmental services. 3i has described the company as the largest vertically integrated waste-services provider in Puerto Rico, with more than 80,000 customers and multiple disposal and transfer assets. The platform has grown through acquisitions, including the 2020 purchase of Republic Services of Puerto Rico and the 2025 acquisition of ARB Waste Services. 3i acquired a majority interest through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in 2021, with management reinvesting alongside the fund.

company.name: Regional Rail, LLC
company.description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. Public disclosures describe a network of more than 875 route miles, 17 railroad operations, and approximately 65,000 annual carloads as of 2023. The footprint expanded materially after 2019 through acquisitions in Florida, the Midwest, Ohio, Indiana, and western Canada. 3i invested in Regional Rail in July 2019 as its North American rail infrastructure platform and remains the disclosed owner.

company.name: Smarte Carte International Holdings, Inc.
company.description: Smarte Carte provides self-service luggage carts, electronic lockers, strollers, mobility services, and related passenger services in airports and other high-traffic venues. Its customer base is concentrated in travel, leisure, and public-venue operators that outsource essential passenger equipment and related services. The company combines an asset-heavy fleet of owned equipment with contracted concession and service arrangements across airports and other locations. Public materials describe more than 140,000 owned units and operations in more than 3,400 locations worldwide. The business has broadened its service offering through acquisitions and contract wins, including Aviation Mobility in 2018, Heathrow trolley operations in 2024, and Lost and Found Software in 2026. 3i invested alongside management in 2017 and continues to hold Smarte Group as a proprietary-capital infrastructure investment; the ownership split is not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Stillhouse Solar Project
company.description: Stillhouse is a utility-scale solar project in Bell County, Texas. Its customer base is the ERCOT market and contracted corporate offtakers, including Hyundai affiliates under a long-term power purchase arrangement. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted generation model centered on long-lived photovoltaic infrastructure. Public disclosures describe a 210 megawatt AC and approximately 281 to 284 megawatt DC solar facility that reached completion in 2025 and commercial operations in 2026. Matrix Renewables acquired the late-stage project from OCI in 2023 and remains the project sponsor. Northleaf Capital Partners became a minority investor through the Stillhouse TEP LLC tax partnership in 2024; Acadia Infrastructure Capital sourced preferred equity and facilitated an environmental-attribute transaction but is not identified as an owner.

milestones.event: Stillhouse Solar Project was founded.
Matrix Renewables acquired the Stillhouse project from OCI Solar Power.

Matrix secured financing for Stillhouse; Northleaf Capital became the Class A investor through Stillhouse TEP LLC, while Acadia sourced preferred equity and facilitated environmental-attribute certificates.
Matrix and SOLV Energy announced completion of Stillhouse Solar in Bell County, Texas.

company.name: Catalyze
company.subsector: Distributed solar, battery storage, and EV charging infrastructure
company.description: Catalyze develops, finances, owns, and operates distributed solar, battery storage, and EV charging assets in the United States. Its customer base includes commercial and industrial real estate owners, business operators, public-sector counterparties, and community-solar subscribers. The company follows an asset-heavy independent power producer and developer model, with revenues supported by long-term contracts, leases, and other recurring project cash flows. Public materials describe a national platform active across more than 30 states, and recent financings support portfolios including 79 MW of New York community-solar projects and 100 MW of projects in New York, Illinois, California, and Virginia. Catalyze was founded in 2017 and has expanded through project development, operating portfolio growth, and structured financing transactions. EnCap invested in 2019, and Actis acquired a co-control stake alongside EnCap in February 2023 through Actis Energy 5; percentage ownership is not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Catalyze was founded as a distributed renewable-energy developer and independent power producer.
EnCap made its initial investment in Catalyze.
Actis and EnCap announced a co-control investment in Catalyze targeting the build-out of roughly 600 MW of solar and storage capacity.
NY Green Bank committed $100 million of financing for a 79 MW community distributed-generation portfolio.
Catalyze closed a 100 MW distributed-solar tax-equity financing with RBC Community Investments.

company.name: TERRANOVA
company.description: TERRANOVA is a Latin American hyperscale data center platform being developed for cloud, AI, and enterprise computing demand. Its end markets are hyperscale cloud providers and other large digital infrastructure users that require large sites with secured land and power. The operating model is asset-heavy and development led, with value creation tied to site control, power access, construction, and eventual long-term customer occupancy. Actis disclosed at launch that the platform had secured land and power capable of supporting up to 1 GW across projects in Mexico, Brazil, and Chile, with the first campus located in Querétaro. Actis launched TERRANOVA in December 2025 through its digital infrastructure strategy, and the current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Valia Energía
company.subsector: Independent power generation and gas transportation
company.description: Valia Energía is a Mexican independent power producer operating natural gas-fired combined-cycle generation assets and a related gas pipeline. Its customers are power purchasers in Mexico's electricity market and other users of reliable dispatchable generation rather than retail end users. The operating model is asset-heavy and infrastructure based, with cash flows tied to large-scale generating plants and associated fuel transportation assets. Actis and company materials state that the platform has 3.2 GW of installed capacity across seven plants and a 58-kilometer gas pipeline. Actis created the platform in 2022 through the acquisition of MT Falcon and expanded it in 2023 through the acquisition of EVM Energia; the current ownership percentage is not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Alpha Generation, LLC
company.subsector: Thermal generation infrastructure and independent power production
company.description: AlphaGen manages and operates a large portfolio of gas- and oil-fired generation assets in major U.S. power markets. Its customer base is primarily wholesale power, capacity, and ancillary-services markets across PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, and CAISO rather than retail end users. The platform follows an asset-heavy model built around dispatchable generating facilities and associated development, repowering, and grid-upgrade opportunities. Public disclosures describe approximately 13 to 14 gigawatts of capacity across 23 to 24 facilities in six states and nearly $2 billion of annual revenue at formation. The portfolio is concentrated in strategic markets where reliability, peaking capacity, and time-to-power have gained importance as electricity demand has risen. ArcLight created AlphaGen in January 2024, and ADIA agreed a $500 million minority investment in January 2025; a 2026 New York regulatory ruling identifies ArcLight Fund VII as the controlling sponsor and discloses ADIA's indirect 16.8% interest through Black Volt B 2024 LLC.

milestones.event: AlphaGen completed $3.7 billion of inaugural corporate financing.
ArcLight created AlphaGen to manage its U.S. power infrastructure portfolio.
ADIA agreed a $500 million minority investment in AlphaGen.
CPP Investments announced a $1.0 billion investment in AlphaGen.
ArcLight stated that AlphaGen would oversee approximately 14 GW of power infrastructure across four U.S. markets.
Public disclosures also described the managed portfolio as generating nearly $2 billion of annual revenue.
Alpha Generation (AlphaGen) was founded.
ArcLight announced the formation of Alpha Generation as an ArcLight-owned platform to oversee its power infrastructure portfolio.

canonicalAfterImage.subsector: Thermal generation infrastructure and independent power production
canonicalAfterImage.description: AlphaGen manages and operates a large portfolio of gas- and oil-fired generation assets in major U.S. power markets. Its customer base is primarily wholesale power, capacity, and ancillary-services markets across PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, and CAISO rather than retail end users. The platform follows an asset-heavy model built around dispatchable generating facilities and associated development, repowering, and grid-upgrade opportunities. Public disclosures describe approximately 13 to 14 gigawatts of capacity across 23 to 24 facilities in six states and nearly $2 billion of annual revenue at formation. The portfolio is concentrated in strategic markets where reliability, peaking capacity, and time-to-power have gained importance as electricity demand has risen. ArcLight created AlphaGen in January 2024, and ADIA agreed a $500 million minority investment in January 2025; a 2026 New York regulatory ruling identifies ArcLight Fund VII as the controlling sponsor and discloses ADIA's indirect 16.8% interest through Black Volt B 2024 LLC.

E.ON secured tax-equity financing from Allianz Capital Partners and State Street in May 2016 in exchange for partial interests in the project. company.name: Great Western Wind Farm
company.description: Great Western Wind Farm is a 225 MW onshore wind project in Ellis and Woodward counties, Oklahoma, that began commercial operations in December 2016 and sells output to Google under a long-term power purchase agreement. company.description: Future Energy Park is a proposed low-carbon fuels development in Calgary, Alberta, led by Green Impact Partners. company.name: Circle Power Renewables
company.description: Circle Power Renewables is a U.S. renewable energy development platform focused on solar, wind and battery-storage projects, principally in Michigan and other regional power markets. Amber Infrastructure and the principals of Circle Power launched the platform in May 2021 after an earlier joint venture; Hunt's 2024 sustainability report identifies Circle Power Renewables as majority Amber-owned, and Amber's current energy-investment materials continue to list the platform as a U.S. investment. Utilities and wholesale power counterparties are its primary end markets. The platform develops projects through dedicated project companies rather than counting each underlying project as a separate manager-level portfolio company: Groveland Mine Solar is owned by Copper Country Power I LLC, a wholly owned Circle Power subsidiary, while 7 Mile Pit Solar is held through a Circle Power project company.

company.name: Iowa RNG
company.description: Iowa RNG is a three-dairy renewable natural gas development in northwest Iowa led by Green Impact Partners. In February 2023 GIP announced a conditional strategic agreement under which Amber Infrastructure was expected to invest in 50% of the project. company.name: Noventa Energy Partners
company.subsector: Wastewater energy transfer and thermal networks
company.description: Noventa Energy Partners developed and operated wastewater energy transfer systems that provided low-carbon heating and cooling to institutional and commercial buildings under long-term energy-as-a-service structures. The asset-heavy platform built district-scale thermal systems connected to wastewater networks. Ancala acquired a majority interest through Ancala Infrastructure Fund III in 2023, while the Canada Infrastructure Bank announced a C$100 million commitment to support Canadian deployment. Noventa Energy Partners Inc. and six related Noventa Group entities entered bankruptcy effective March 20, 2026, and MNP was appointed as licensed insolvency trustee. Noventa is therefore no longer treated as an active operating platform or current Ancala portfolio company.

company.name: Phoenix Rail
company.description: Phoenix Rail is a Denver-headquartered short-line freight rail and intermodal platform formed by Ancala Partners and Arkadia Rail Partners to acquire and grow regional rail infrastructure across the United States. The company owns and operates railroads and rail-related businesses serving more than 100 customers across consumer products, plastics, metals, agriculture, building products, food and chemicals. Its wholly owned subsidiary, Lehigh Valley Rail Management, operates a 61-mile freight rail network and intermodal terminal in Pennsylvania with access to Norfolk Southern, CSX and CPKC. Phoenix Rail completed the LVRM acquisition on January 28, 2025, and Ancala publicly describes its interest in the platform as a significant controlling stake; no exact percentage or fund vehicle is publicly disclosed.

company.name: Valentra
company.subsector: Formalin production and chemical pipeline infrastructure
company.description: Valentra is a U.S. Gulf Coast producer of formalin products and operator of associated chemical infrastructure. Its pipeline-connected sites in Baytown, Texas; Luling, Louisiana; and Geismar, Louisiana combine production, storage, pipelines, rail access and barge docks to supply co-located chemical plants and offsite industrial customers under large-volume, multi-year contracts. Its products support agriculture, healthcare, automotive, construction, resins, paints and coatings, consumer goods and other industrial end markets. Ancala Partners acquired the business from Hexion and formed Valentra as a standalone platform on December 4, 2025. Financial terms, Ancala's exact stake and its fund vehicle were not publicly disclosed.

company.name: PearlX
company.subsector: Multifamily distributed solar, battery storage and smart-grid infrastructure
company.description: PearlX Infrastructure LLC develops, finances, owns and operates distributed solar, battery-storage and related electrification systems at multifamily properties in the United States. The Charlottesville-based platform installs and maintains the infrastructure without upfront property-owner capital, provides participating residents discounted on-site electricity and pays landlords for use of property space. Founded in 2019, PearlX has operated principally in California and Texas. Antin Infrastructure Partners acquired a majority stake through Antin NextGen Fund I in early 2023. Antin disclosed in March 2026 that it had decided in December 2025 to fully exit the investment; no buyer or completed closing was publicly identified as of August 7, 2026.

milestones.event: Michael Huerta and Peter Mendonez founded PearlX Infrastructure.
Antin Infrastructure Partners acquired a majority stake in PearlX through Antin NextGen Fund I.
Antin decided to fully exit its NextGen Fund I investment in PearlX; the buyer and completed closing were not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Doral Renewables LLC
company.description: Doral Renewables develops, owns, and operates utility-scale solar and storage projects in the United States. Its customer base consists of utilities, corporate offtakers, and wholesale power markets that contract for power, renewable attributes, and grid services. The business follows an asset-heavy independent power producer model with a large development pipeline and direct ownership of utility-scale projects. Public disclosures describe a development portfolio of more than 13 gigawatts across 18 states, anchored by the multi-phase Mammoth Solar development in Indiana. The company combines project development, financing, construction, and long-term ownership, with a focus on utility-scale and agrivoltaic projects. APG invested $400 million on behalf of ABP in 2024 and was described as the largest individual shareholder following the closing.

milestones.event: Global Energy Generation LLC was formed on August 28, 2019; it later adopted the legal name Doral Renewables LLC and the Doral LLC trade name.
Doral announced a $400 million minority equity investment from APG.
Doral completed APG's $400 million minority investment on behalf of ABP; the investor received 40% of Doral's membership interests, subject to contractual adjustment provisions.

company.name: Duquesne Light Company
company.description: Duquesne Light Company is the regulated electric transmission and distribution utility serving more than 600,000 customers across Allegheny and Beaver counties, including Pittsburgh, over an approximately 812-square-mile service territory. The company does not generate power and maintains approximately 8,400 miles of transmission and distribution lines. Its parent, DQE Holdings LLC, discloses three current ownership vehicles: GIC affiliate Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. at 44.4%, Manulife/John Hancock and PGGM vehicle Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC at 30.4%, and APG/CalSTRS vehicle AIA Montana LLC, managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, at 25.2%. Macquarie's former infrastructure ownership was realized in 2016.

milestones.event: The present Duquesne Light Company was formed on November 15, 1912 through the consolidation of three predecessor utilities.
Duquesne Light Holdings completed its take-private by a Macquarie-led infrastructure consortium in May 2007.
Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd., a GIC affiliate, acquired DUET's interests in DQE Holdings; Duquesne reports GIC as an owner since 2011 and its current stake as 44.4%.
Macquarie Infrastructure and Real Assets sold its 30.4% DQE Holdings interest to PGGM and John Hancock through Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC.
AIA Montana LLC, owned by APG Americas Infrastructure and CalSTRS and managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, became a DQE Holdings owner; its current vehicle interest is 25.2%.

company.name: Gemini Solar + Storage
company.description: Gemini Solar + Storage is an operating 690 MWac solar photovoltaic and 380 MW / approximately 1,416 MWh battery storage project in Clark County, Nevada, developed by Quinbrook with its portfolio company Primergy. The co-located facility supplies NV Energy under a 25-year power purchase agreement and is designed to meet approximately 10% of Nevada's peak power demand. APG acquired a 49% interest on behalf of ABP in 2022. In April 2024, Quinbrook's Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP acquired the remaining 51%, and the project reached full commercial operations in 2024. A February 2026 refinancing continued to identify the same 51% Quinbrook / 49% APG ownership structure.

milestones.event: Quinbrook acquired the Gemini project and began its development with portfolio company Primergy.
The U.S. Department of the Interior approved Solar Partners XI LLC's plan to construct the 690 MW Gemini Solar Project on federal land northeast of Las Vegas.
APG acquired a 49% equity interest in Gemini on behalf of pension fund client ABP during construction.
Quinbrook's Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP acquired a 51% interest in Gemini from Quinbrook's Low Carbon Power Fund and other equity holders; APG retained 49%.
Primergy and Quinbrook announced that Gemini had reached full commercial operations in Clark County, Nevada.

company.name: Hawaiʻi Gas
company.subsector: Regulated gas utility and propane distribution
company.description: Hawaiʻi Gas is the only government-franchised full-service gas utility in Hawaiʻi and a statewide propane distributor. Founded in 1904, it manufactures and distributes synthetic and renewable natural gas to utility customers on Oʻahu and supplies liquefied petroleum gas to residential and commercial customers across the state's six primary islands. Its operating base includes approximately 1,100 miles of pipeline, bulk storage, and delivery fleets. The company is wholly owned by funds managed by Argo through AMF Hawaiʻi Investment Holdings, LLC; APG Infrastructure Pool 2020-2021 disclosed Hawaiʻi Gas as an infrastructure investment following the July 2022 acquisition.

milestones.event: Honolulu Gas Company, the predecessor of Hawaiʻi Gas, was founded.
Hawaiʻi Gas announced that Argo Infrastructure Partners would acquire the company from Macquarie Infrastructure Corporation, subject to regulatory approval.
The Hawaiʻi Public Utilities Commission approved the transfer of control to AMF Hawaii Holdings, LLC in Decision and Order No. 38478.
Argo Infrastructure Partners completed its acquisition of Hawaiʻi Gas through an affiliated investment vehicle backed by institutional capital including APG.
Isle Gas, another wholly owned AMF subsidiary serviced by Hawaiʻi Gas, completed its acquisition of AmeriGas's Hawaiʻi propane storage and delivery assets.

company.name: Hudson Transmission Project
company.description: Hudson Transmission Project is a 660 MW, 7.1-mile high-voltage direct-current merchant transmission link between Ridgefield, New Jersey and Manhattan. Hudson Transmission Partners, LLC owns the project and PowerBridge operates it; 575 MW, or 87.12% of capacity, is contracted to the New York Power Authority through June 2033. The line entered commercial service in June 2013. AMF Oratam Investments LLC, managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, acquired the project's 94% Class C economic interest in March 2019. APG Infrastructure Pool 2014 participates indirectly through Sogra Investment Holding B.V. and disclosed Hudson Transmission Partners as 6% of pool assets for 2022; current beneficial ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Construction began on the Hudson Transmission Project's underground and underwater HVDC link between New Jersey and Manhattan.
The 660 MW Hudson Transmission Project entered commercial service ahead of schedule.
Ares EIF and Starwood Energy agreed to sell their Hudson interests to AMF Oratam Investments LLC, an Argo-managed investment vehicle.
Argo's AMF Oratam investment vehicle completed the acquisition of the 94% Class C economic interest in Hudson Transmission Partners for institutional investors including APG.

company.name: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC
company.description: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC is the private concessionaire and operator of the 66 Express Outside the Beltway managed lanes in Northern Virginia, also known as Transform 66 Outside the Beltway. Under a 50-year DBFOM agreement with the Virginia Department of Transportation through 2066, the company financed, delivered, operates, and maintains a 22.5-mile corridor from I-495 to Route 29 in Gainesville. The approximately $3.7 billion project includes two express lanes and three rebuilt general-purpose lanes in each direction, interchange upgrades, more than 4,000 park-and-ride spaces, transit funding, and 18 miles of shared-use path. The full corridor opened ahead of schedule in November 2022. Ferrovial's audited 2025 filing reports Cintra at 55.7%, Meridiam Infrastructure S.a.r.l. at 29.75%, and I-66 Blocker (APG) at 14.55%.

Cintra completed the acquisition of an additional 5.704% interest from John Laing, increasing its controlling stake in the I-66 concession to 55.704%.
The western nine-mile section of the 66 Express Lanes opened ahead of schedule between Gainesville and Route 28 in Centreville.
Transform 66 Outside the Beltway opened to traffic.
The full 22.5-mile 66 Express Outside the Beltway corridor opened to traffic ahead of schedule.
The final section of the new express lanes opened. (Operations)
The consortium marked the first full year of operations.

company.name: LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC
company.description: LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC is the concession company and TIFIA borrower for LBJ Express, a managed-lanes toll concession in Dallas County, Texas. Under a 52-year DBFOM comprehensive development agreement with the Texas Department of Transportation through 2061, the company financed, reconstructed, operates, and maintains approximately 13.25 miles of I-635 and I-35E, including dynamically priced managed lanes alongside rebuilt general-purpose and frontage roads. The project reached financial close in June 2010, began construction in January 2011, and fully opened in September 2015. Ferrovial's SEC-filed May 2026 factbook reports Cintra at 54.60%, APG at 28.33%, and Meridiam at 17.07%; Meridiam's current portfolio page identifies the corresponding non-Cintra vehicles as LBJ Blocker and MI LBJ.

milestones.event: TxDOT executed the 52-year comprehensive development agreement with LBJ Infrastructure Group, formerly LBJ Development Partners, for the IH 635 managed-lanes concession.
LBJ Infrastructure Group reached financial close for the LBJ Express concession one day after executing its $850 million TIFIA credit agreement.
Construction began on the LBJ Express managed-lanes project.
APG joined the LBJ Express concession by acquiring an ownership interest from Meridiam.
LBJ Express reached substantial completion with all lanes open to traffic.
Cintra, APG, and Meridiam acquired the Dallas Police and Fire Pension System's remaining LBJ interest; the resulting ownership was Cintra 54.60%, APG 28.33%, and Meridiam 17.07%.
The concession completed a refinancing that included approximately $615 million of tax-exempt private activity bonds replacing the original 2010 bonds.
The LBJ Express consortium marked ten years since the managed-lanes project opened to traffic.

company.name: Pattern Energy Group LP
company.subsector: Wind, solar, storage, and transmission development
company.description: Pattern Energy Group LP is a San Francisco-headquartered developer, owner, and operator of utility-scale wind, solar, energy storage, and transmission infrastructure across North America. The company reports 46 operating facilities totaling approximately 12 GW and a 40 GW development and active-construction portfolio. CPP Investments has owned the platform since the March 2020 take-private and holds 69.1% after Pattern completed its share-based acquisition of CPP-owned Cordelio Power on April 2, 2026. On June 9, 2025, an APG- and ART-headed consortium that also included a CalSTRS buyer vehicle acquired Riverstone's entire stake alongside Pattern management; the individual consortium and management stakes were not disclosed. Riverstone had backed Pattern since its 2009 formation and rolled its interest through the 2020 combination before exiting in 2025.

company.name: SP Solar Holdings I, LP
company.subsector: Contracted utility-scale solar and battery storage portfolio
company.description: SP Solar Holdings I, LP is a Delaware limited partnership that indirectly owns substantially all of Southern Power's solar and battery energy storage facilities. Southern Power controls the partnership through wholly owned subsidiaries, holds 67%, and operates and maintains the assets; APG holds the 33% passive limited-partner interest through Scarlet Renewables LLC after acquiring it from Global Atlantic in November 2023. The assets supply utilities and other power purchasers under long-term contracts across multiple U.S. states. Southern Company's June 2026 filing continued to report the 67%/33% economics and Southern Power control, while APG's March 2026 regulatory filing continued to list Scarlet Renewables as an APG-managed infrastructure vehicle.

Southern Power announced battery storage additions at selected California solar projects within the broader portfolio.
Southern Power acquired the Millers Branch Solar Facility in Texas, expanding its broader solar fleet.
At APG's investment, the disclosed portfolio comprised 26 operating solar facilities and two battery storage projects totaling approximately 2.2 GW across six U.S. states.
Global Atlantic announced that it had completed the sale of its 33% SP Solar interest to APG; Southern Power remained the majority owner and operator.

company.name: Brightspeed
company.ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (including AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P.)
company.description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure across 20 U.S. states from Charlotte, North Carolina. Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier operations in October 2022. The FCC's 2022 approval order for the subsequently consummated acquisition shows that the Apollo ownership group included AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P., a vehicle of Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II, with a direct interest of less than 5% alongside larger Apollo private-equity and co-invest vehicles; the 2% equity and 3% voting values appeared only in the December 2023 proposed post-Mubadala structure. Mubadala signed a $500 million minority investment through CEPSA Holding LLC in May 2023, and the FCC approved the proposed foreign-ownership structure in December 2023; no public legal-closing announcement or date was found, so Mubadala remains a signed pending incoming investor in this census. Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization in August 2024 that issued warrants and preferred stock, and the current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. No Apollo or Mubadala exit was found through August 8, 2026.

milestones.event: Apollo-managed private-equity funds announced an agreement to acquire Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier business in 20 U.S. states.
Brightspeed unveiled its brand for the pending Apollo acquisition of Lumen's ILEC operations.
Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition from Lumen and Brightspeed began operating the business.
Mubadala and Brightspeed announced a signed $500 million minority investment subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions; no public legal-closing date was found.

The FCC approved Brightspeed's proposed post-Mubadala foreign-ownership structure, which showed pro forma interests of 2% equity for AIOF II and approximately 28% proposed equity for Mubadala through CEPSA Holding LLC.

Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization that secured approximately $3.7 billion of new financing, eliminated approximately $1.1 billion of debt and issued warrants and preferred stock to participating lenders.

The FCC's 2022 approval order for the subsequently consummated acquisition shows that the Apollo ownership group included AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P., a vehicle of Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II, with a direct interest of less than 5% alongside larger Apollo private-equity and co-invest vehicles; the 2% equity and 3% voting values appeared only in the December 2023 proposed post-Mubadala structure. Mubadala signed a $500 million minority investment through CEPSA Holding LLC in May 2023, and the FCC approved the proposed foreign-ownership structure in December 2023; no public legal-closing announcement or date was found, so Mubadala remains a signed pending incoming investor in this census. Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization in August 2024 that issued warrants and preferred stock, and the current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. No Apollo or Mubadala exit was found through August 8, 2026.

company.name: Broad Reach Power
company.description: Broad Reach Power was a Houston-based utility-scale battery storage and renewable-energy platform founded by EnCap Energy Transition in 2019. Apollo-managed infrastructure funds collectively acquired a 50% stake in December 2021 alongside the EnCap-led shareholder group. Apollo confirms that Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II participated, but its individual allocation was not publicly disclosed. EnCap and Apollo announced the sale of Broad Reach Power's battery-storage business to ENGIE in August 2023, excluding 1.8 GW of solar and wind projects and 4 GWh of Mountain West battery projects from the transaction perimeter. ENGIE finalized its acquisition of 100% of Broad Reach Power from EnCap and Apollo in October 2023 and fully consolidated the acquired business. ENGIE's audited 2025 financial statements continue to report 100% ownership of Group Broad Reach Power, while EnCap classifies Broad Reach Power as realized in 2023. No current Apollo ownership or subsequent reacquisition was found through August 8, 2026. Public sources reviewed do not disclose the post-closing ownership or operating identity of the excluded Mountain West portfolio.

company.name: Apollo–Bullrock Community Solar Joint Venture
company.ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (specific funds and legal vehicle not publicly disclosed)
company.description: The Apollo–Bullrock Community Solar Joint Venture is a 2025 equity partnership formed by Apollo-managed funds and Bullrock Energy Ventures to invest in and develop a portfolio of community solar assets across New York and New England. Apollo committed up to $220 million in equity, including $100 million to support development of Bullrock's nearly 500 MW renewable-energy pipeline. Bullrock remains the separate developer and operating partner; reviewed sources do not establish that Apollo acquired an interest in the Bullrock corporate parent. Current July 2026 FINRA disclosures identify AP Bullrock Holdings and Delphi Bullrock Energy Ventures LLC as Apollo-affiliated portfolio companies, corroborating the joint venture's active status. The specific Apollo funds, deployed amount, ownership percentage, separate legal closing date and entity chain are not publicly disclosed. No sale or Apollo exit was identified through August 8, 2026.

milestones.event: Bullrock Solar, the operating predecessor of joint-venture partner Bullrock Energy Ventures, was founded as a vertically integrated solar developer offering development, construction, operations and asset-management capabilities.

Bullrock and NxtGen Solar formed an earlier project joint venture and jointly developed a 150 MW community-solar portfolio, establishing the operating partnership that later became Bullrock Energy Ventures.
Bullrock, the joint venture's developer and operating partner, built its investment-management division to raise and manage external capital for solar development and expansion.
Bullrock Energy Ventures, the joint venture's separate operating partner, launched its first fund to scale its community-solar portfolio and invest in adjacent renewable-energy businesses.

Apollo-managed funds and Bullrock Energy Ventures formed an equity joint venture for a New York and New England community-solar portfolio, with Apollo committing up to $220 million, including $100 million for development of Bullrock's nearly 500 MW pipeline.

company.description: Freedom Alternative Fuel Infrastructure, branded Freedom AFI and formerly known as Freedom CNG, designs, builds, owns and operates fixed and mobile compressed-natural-gas and renewable-natural-gas fueling infrastructure across the United States and Canada. The Houston-headquartered platform serves fleets including logistics and transportation operators, refuse companies, municipalities and school districts. Founded in 2012, Freedom expanded its Western U.S. network through the 2025 acquisitions of X3CNG and Lancer Energy and added Canadian capabilities through ComTech Energy. Apollo Global Management-managed funds acquired a majority interest in September 2024; the exact ownership percentage and specific fund are not publicly disclosed. Current company and Apollo materials continued to show Apollo majority ownership and Infrastructure Group board representation, and no Apollo exit was identified through August 8, 2026.

company.ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (specific funds and legal vehicle not publicly disclosed)
company.description: GFL Environmental Services (GES) is a North American environmental-infrastructure services platform providing liquid-waste management, soil remediation, used-oil re-refining, field and industrial services, waste processing and recycling, and specialized transportation. The company serves more than 50,000 customers through more than 260 locations and a specialized fleet of more than 5,500 assets. GES became an independent joint-venture platform effective March 1, 2025 in a transaction valued at C$8.0 billion. Following HPS Investment Partners' September 3, 2025 equity subscription, GFL Environmental Inc. retained approximately 34%, while Apollo-managed funds, BC-managed funds and HPS-managed funds each held approximately 22%. Apollo stated that its investment included capital from its Infrastructure and Hybrid Value strategies.

milestones.event: The environmental-services operations were developed within GFL before being separated into the independent GES platform.

GFL announced a definitive C$8.0 billion transaction with Apollo-managed and BC-managed funds for its Environmental Services business; Apollo attributed its investment to its Infrastructure and Hybrid Value strategies.
The transaction became effective and established GES as an independent joint venture, with Apollo and BC each holding approximately 28% and GFL retaining approximately 44%.
HPS Investment Partners subscribed for approximately 22% of GES, diluting GFL to approximately 34% and Apollo and BC to approximately 22% each.

canonicalAfterImage.description: Intermodal Tank Transport (ITT) is a Houston-headquartered, U.S.-based global provider of ISO-tank container transportation, logistics and depot services for bulk-liquid chemical and food-grade supply chains. Founded in Medellin in 1993, ITT arranges end-to-end transport across major modes, operates a tank fleet and provides maintenance, cleaning and inspection through a global office and depot network. Apollo Infrastructure Funds announced a structured equity investment in June 2023; later Apollo filings and portfolio materials support closed-active ownership, but the exact stake, broader legal closing date and specific current fund or vehicle are not publicly disclosed. ITT acquired Bulk Tainer Group in August 2025, and no Apollo exit was identified through August 8, 2026.

company.name: Nokomis Energy
company.ownershipVehicle: Great Bay Renewables royalty financing; no direct Nokomis ownership established
company.description: Nokomis Energy, LLC is a Minneapolis-based distributed-solar developer founded in 2017. Great Bay Renewables closed a royalty-financing transaction in June 2024 through Nokomis Bay LLC, a separate holding company jointly held by Great Bay and Nokomis. Great Bay received Class R units in that royalty structure, project-level gross-revenue royalties, and unexercised warrants permitting a future acquisition of up to 10% of Nokomis Energy. Reviewed public sources do not establish exercise of the warrants or current direct Apollo ownership of Nokomis Energy. Apollo-managed funds sold their upstream 50% Great Bay interest to Northampton Capital Partners on July 30, 2026. Because the manager exposure was indirect royalty financing rather than direct company ownership, Nokomis is excluded from the manager-level PortCo census.

company.name: Summit Ridge Energy
company.ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (specific fund and legal vehicle not publicly disclosed)
company.description: Summit Ridge Energy develops, constructs, owns, and operates distributed solar and battery-storage systems across the U.S. Midwest, Mid-Atlantic, and New England. Founded in 2017, the company reported more than 275 facilities and over 3 GW of operating and development-stage solar and storage projects in July 2026. Apollo-managed funds made a $175 million strategic platform investment in 2022; the exact Apollo stake, fund and legal vehicle are not publicly disclosed. On July 14, 2026, Global Infrastructure Partners, a part of BlackRock, agreed through its mid-market infrastructure strategy to acquire a majority and controlling interest, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. No closing announcement was identified through August 12, 2026, so Apollo remains the current legal owner and GIP is recorded only as a signed pending counterparty. Apollo's separate 2025 commitment of up to $400 million relates to an Illinois solar-asset joint venture rather than a second corporate ownership period.

milestones.event: Summit Ridge Energy was founded.
Apollo funds announced a $175 million strategic investment in Summit Ridge Energy.
Summit Ridge and Bank of America closed a $305 million credit facility for a solar portfolio.
Apollo funds committed up to $400 million for a new commercial solar partnership with Summit Ridge.
Summit Ridge announced a $290 million facility with MUFG and stated that it had raised more than $5 billion for over 200 solar facilities since launch.

company.description: Alpha Generation, LLC (AlphaGen) owns and operates 26 dispatchable power-generation facilities totaling approximately 14 GW across six U.S. states and the PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE and CAISO markets. ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII formed AlphaGen in January 2024 and remains the controlling majority owner. ADIA holds a separately evidenced 16.8% indirect interest through Black Volt B 2024 LLC. Exact ArcLight and CPP ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed, and no subsequent exit or pending sale was identified through August 12, 2026.

company.name: Catalyst Old River Hydroelectric Limited Partnership
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Renewable Infrastructure Fund SM SPV, L.P.
company.description: Catalyst Old River Hydroelectric Limited Partnership owns and operates the 192 MW Sidney A. Murray Jr. Hydroelectric Station on a diversion of the Mississippi River near Vidalia, Louisiana. The run-of-river facility entered service in 1990 and sells power to an Entergy utility and the Town of Vidalia under long-term arrangements extending through 2031. Brookfield Renewable affiliates hold the 75% economic balance and the managing/control position. ArcLight Capital Partners holds the remaining 25% through ArcLight Renewable Infrastructure Fund SM SPV, L.P., which acquired the interest from ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V on July 8, 2021. The project company is the single PortCo; its upstream holdcos, co-licensee and lenders are not separate owners.

ArcLight Renewable Infrastructure Fund SM SPV, L.P. acquired a 25% interest in the project from ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V, L.P.

company.name: Chief Power
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V, L.P.
company.description: Chief Power is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V-backed merchant-generation platform holding partial tenant-in-common interests in the Keystone and Conemaugh coal-fired generating stations in western Pennsylvania. ArcLight established the platform in 2014 and expanded it through a separately financed acquisition in 2019. After a 2020 lender restructuring transferred control of the original tranche, Fund V retained a small minority voting interest and continued to control the separately owned Chief Power Finance II tranche. Current public filings identify Fund V as holding greater than 10% voting interests in each II plant-owner entity, while the exact Fund V economic percentage is not publicly disclosed. Chief Power is the single PortCo; its financing entities, transfer parent, plant-owner subsidiaries and the two jointly owned generating stations are not separate portfolio companies.

milestones.event: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V completed the acquisition of Exelon's 41.98% Keystone and 31.28% Conemaugh ownership interests and established the Chief Power platform.
Chief Power acquired additional minority interests, increasing its original tranche to 44.45% of Keystone and 35.11% of Conemaugh.
ArcLight's separately financed Chief II entities completed the acquisition of PSEG's 22.84% Keystone and 22.5% Conemaugh interests.

A lender restructuring transferred control of the original Chief Power Finance tranche to Chief Power Transfer Parent; Fund V retained a small interest subsequently reported at approximately 3%, while the separate Chief Power Finance II tranche remained outside the transfer and under ArcLight control.

company.name: Takanock, LLC
company.ownershipVehicle: Jointly managed ArcLight / DigitalBridge investment vehicle
company.description: Takanock, LLC develops power-enabled sites and permanent on-site generation for data centers in power-constrained U.S. markets. The Traverse City-based platform combines land, entitlements, generation, fuel supply and grid interconnection to accelerate time to power for hyperscale and other large data-center customers, with disclosed activity including Northern Virginia and Phoenix. The operating business was formed in 2023, and the current Delaware LLC was formed in 2025. ArcLight and DigitalBridge became collective majority owners in an April 2025 equity financing and announced aggregate commitments of up to US$500 million on June 25, 2025; original investors retained a collective minority interest. Each sponsor's individual percentage, ArcLight fund and exact joint investment vehicle are not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Gulf Coast Express Pipeline LLC (GCX)
company.description: Gulf Coast Express Pipeline LLC (GCX) is an approximately 500-mile natural-gas transmission system that moves Permian Basin production from the Waha area to Agua Dulce and other South Texas markets. The system is fully subscribed under long-term binding transportation agreements and has approximately 2.59 Bcf/d of capacity following a June 2026 compression expansion. Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline LLC owns 34% and operates GCX. ArcLight-managed vehicles own the remaining 66% through three separately recorded tranches acquired in 2022, 2024 and 2025. Mubadala's publicly disclosed co-investment is nested within ArcLight's 2025 tranche; its specific percentage and legal vehicle are not publicly disclosed and are not additive to ArcLight's 66% aggregate interest. No GCX-specific sale or pending exit was identified through August 13, 2026.

milestones.event: Kinder Morgan, DCP Midstream and Targa reached final investment decision for the approximately $1.7 billion Gulf Coast Express Pipeline after securing long-term binding transportation commitments.
Altus Midstream exercised its option to acquire a 15% GCX interest, leaving Kinder Morgan with 35% and DCP Midstream and Targa with 25% each.
GCX entered full commercial service ahead of schedule with approximately 2.0 Bcf/d of capacity fully subscribed under long-term contracts.
ArcLight completed its $857 million acquisition of Targa's 25% GCX interest through AL GCX Holdings LLC.
ArcLight completed its acquisition of Kinetik's 16% GCX interest for $510 million upfront plus a $30 million deferred payment.
GCX reached final investment decision for an approximately $455 million compression expansion designed to add 570 MMcf/d of capacity under binding long-term agreements.
Phillips 66 entered into a definitive agreement to sell its 25% non-operated GCX interest to an ArcLight affiliate for $865 million.
Phillips 66 closed the sale of its 25% GCX interest to the ArcLight affiliate for $853 million of cash proceeds.
ArcLight publicly announced completion of the 25% acquisition and identified Mubadala as its partner in acquiring an interest in GCX.
GCX placed its approximately $450 million expansion in service, adding approximately 570 MMcf/d and increasing total system capacity to approximately 2.59 Bcf/d.

canonicalAfterImage.name: Gulf Coast Express Pipeline LLC (GCX)
canonicalAfterImage.description: Gulf Coast Express Pipeline LLC (GCX) is an approximately 500-mile natural-gas transmission system that moves Permian Basin production from the Waha area to Agua Dulce and other South Texas markets. The system is fully subscribed under long-term binding transportation agreements and has approximately 2.59 Bcf/d of capacity following a June 2026 compression expansion. Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline LLC owns 34% and operates GCX. ArcLight-managed vehicles own the remaining 66% through three separately recorded tranches acquired in 2022, 2024 and 2025. Mubadala's publicly disclosed co-investment is nested within ArcLight's 2025 tranche; its specific percentage and legal vehicle are not publicly disclosed and are not additive to ArcLight's 66% aggregate interest. No GCX-specific sale or pending exit was identified through August 13, 2026.

milestones.event: Kinder Morgan, DCP Midstream and Targa reached final investment decision for the approximately $1.7 billion Gulf Coast Express Pipeline after securing long-term binding transportation commitments.
Altus Midstream exercised its option to acquire a 15% GCX interest, leaving Kinder Morgan with 35% and DCP Midstream and Targa with 25% each.
GCX entered full commercial service ahead of schedule with approximately 2.0 Bcf/d of capacity fully subscribed under long-term contracts.
ArcLight completed its $857 million acquisition of Targa's 25% GCX interest through AL GCX Holdings LLC.
ArcLight completed its acquisition of Kinetik's 16% GCX interest for $510 million upfront plus a $30 million deferred payment.
GCX reached final investment decision for an approximately $455 million compression expansion designed to add 570 MMcf/d of capacity under binding long-term agreements.
Phillips 66 entered into a definitive agreement to sell its 25% non-operated GCX interest to an ArcLight affiliate for $865 million.
Phillips 66 closed the sale of its 25% GCX interest to the ArcLight affiliate for $853 million of cash proceeds.
ArcLight publicly announced completion of the 25% acquisition and identified Mubadala as its partner in acquiring an interest in GCX.
GCX placed its approximately $450 million expansion in service, adding approximately 570 MMcf/d and increasing total system capacity to approximately 2.59 Bcf/d.

company.description: Inspiration Mobility Group is a Washington, D.C.-headquartered sustainable infrastructure platform that finances, owns, develops and operates commercial electric-vehicle fleets, charging systems and related energy assets across North America. Its operating businesses include Inspiration Fleet and Inspiration Energy. ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII launched the platform in 2021 with an initial $200 million commitment; Macquarie Asset Management and Ferrovial supplied a further $215 million of capital that closed in May 2022. Current company and investor materials identify ArcLight, Macquarie and Ferrovial as continuing investors, while their exact ownership percentages and Macquarie and Ferrovial investment vehicles are not publicly disclosed. company.name: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
company.description: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC (NGPL) is a major U.S. interstate natural-gas transmission and storage company serving producers, utilities, marketers, power generators, industrial users and LNG-linked markets. Kinder Morgan's audited 2025 reporting lists approximately 9,105 miles of pipeline, 8.40 Bcf/d of design capacity and 288 Bcf of storage capacity. The network spans nine states and connects major U.S. supply basins with Midwest demand centers and Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast markets. NGPL provides firm, flexible-firm and interruptible transportation, multiple storage products, balancing, park-and-loan and line-pack services. ArcLight-controlled funds own 62.5%, comprising a 37.5% Fund VII interest and a separate 25% investment whose fund and vehicle split is not publicly disclosed, while Kinder Morgan owns 37.5% and operates the system. Brookfield fully exited in May 2025, and no later NGPL-specific sale or pending ownership change was identified through August 13, 2026.

milestones.event: ArcLight completed its initial $830 million acquisition of a 25% NGPL interest from Kinder Morgan and Brookfield Infrastructure; Kinder Morgan and Brookfield each retained 37.5%.
ArcLight acquired an additional 12.5% NGPL interest from Brookfield Infrastructure, increasing ArcLight's ownership to 37.5% and reducing Brookfield's interest to 25%.
Brookfield Infrastructure signed an agreement to sell its remaining 25% NGPL interest to an existing owner, describing the transaction as its complete exit from the business.
ArcLight completed the acquisition of Brookfield's remaining 25% NGPL interest, increasing ArcLight-controlled ownership to 62.5%; Kinder Morgan retained 37.5% and continued as operator.

company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI, L.P.
company.description: Orca Acquisitions, LLC is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI and Olympus Power joint-venture platform that indirectly owns Walleye Power, LLC through Walleye Energy Holdings, LLC. Walleye owns and operates the Bay Shore merchant-power and industrial-steam facility in Oregon, Ohio. A June 2026 FERC filing reports 136 MW of summer-rated steam generation and a 16 MW oil-fired unit. ArcLight Orca Holdings, LLC holds 95% of Orca's Class A managing interests, appoints two management-committee members and controls day-to-day decisions. Olympus affiliates hold the remaining 5% of Class A interests and all non-managing, non-voting Class B interests. The exact overall economic ownership split is not publicly disclosed. Orca is the single PortCo; Walleye, its holding company, Bay Shore and the individual generating units are subsidiaries or assets beneath the platform. No Orca-specific sale or pending ownership transfer was identified through August 14, 2026.

milestones.event: An amended and restated LLC agreement dated July 25, 2016 documented Orca Acquisitions' ArcLight and Olympus ownership and governance structure.
Orca subsidiary Walleye entered into an asset-purchase agreement to acquire the Bay Shore Generating Facility from FirstEnergy Solutions affiliates.
Walleye Energy, LLC changed its name to Walleye Power, LLC before the Bay Shore acquisition closed.
Walleye completed the acquisition of the Bay Shore Generating Facility.

ArcLight's current portfolio-services page identifies Phoenix and Thunderbird as the initial Fund VIII operating portfolios managed by SkyVest, while ArcLight's 2025 ESG report reports 467 MW for Phoenix. Phoenix is counted as the manager-level portfolio; SkyVest is the management platform, and individual assets or projects beneath Phoenix are not separate PortCos. ArcLight's live investments page lists Phoenix as Current. Public sources reviewed do not disclose an exact ownership-entry date, stake, website, founding year, headquarters, or a Phoenix-level exit through August 14, 2026.

company.name: TransMontaigne Partners LLC
company.subsector: Bulk liquid storage, terminaling and transportation
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI, L.P.
company.description: TransMontaigne Partners LLC is a Denver-based U.S. midstream infrastructure platform providing terminaling, storage, transportation, blending and related logistics for refined petroleum products, renewable fuels and feedstocks, crude oil, chemicals, fertilizers and other bulk liquids. Its network spans 54 terminal facilities across major U.S. markets. ArcLight acquired platform control through the general partner in February 2016, and ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI completed the take-private in February 2019. TLP Finance Holdings now owns 100% of TransMontaigne and is an indirect wholly owned Fund VI subsidiary. Pike Holdings and Pike Petroleum Holdings are upstream sponsor-shell census labels, not separate PortCos; intermediate holding vehicles, operating subsidiaries and individual assets beneath TransMontaigne are subsumed. No platform-level sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: An ArcLight affiliate completed its $350 million acquisition of TransMontaigne GP and obtained control of the platform; NGL retained public units and its separate marketing business.
TransMontaigne announced a definitive agreement for an indirect ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI subsidiary to acquire the remaining public units for approximately $536 million.
Fund VI's take-private closed, making TransMontaigne wholly owned; the platform converted from TransMontaigne Partners L.P. to TransMontaigne Partners LLC and TLP Finance became sole managing member.

company.name: REC Power
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
company.description: REC Power, formerly REC Solar, is a nationwide independent power producer that develops and acquires, finances, owns, operates and services distributed power assets spanning solar, battery storage, fuel cells, microgrids and gensets for commercial, industrial, institutional and public-sector customers. Founded in 1997, the platform reports more than 700 projects across 29 states and, after a July 2026 acquisition, more than 410 MW of operating assets across 25 states. Duke Energy completed the sale of its commercial distributed-generation business, including REC Solar, to an ArcLight-managed investment fund in October 2023. REC Power states that it remains owned by ArcLight Capital Partners, and ArcLight attributes the investment to Fund VII. Public sources do not disclose the platform-level stake or legal acquisition vehicle.
company.headquarters: San Luis Obispo, California, United States

milestones.event: Judy Staley and Fred Sisson co-founded REC (Renewable Energy Concepts) Solar in California.
Duke Energy completed the sale of its commercial distributed-generation portfolio, including REC Solar, to an investment fund managed by ArcLight Capital Partners.
REC Solar rebranded as REC Power to reflect its broader role as a long-term owner and operator of distributed power resources.
REC Power completed the acquisition of fifteen operating distributed-generation solar projects totaling 68 MW, increasing its operating portfolio to more than 410 MW across 25 states.

company.name: Salamanca Infrastructure LLC
company.subsector: Offshore floating production and export infrastructure
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
company.description: Salamanca Infrastructure LLC is the U.S. midstream infrastructure owner of the Salamanca floating production system and associated oil and natural-gas export laterals at Keathley Canyon Block 689 in the deepwater U.S. Gulf of Mexico. The refurbished semi-submersible receives production from the separate Leon and Castile upstream fields and can process 60,000 barrels of oil per day and 40 million cubic feet of natural gas per day. LLOG operates the facility but is not treated as a manager-level owner. ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII-backed affiliates financed the development through an ownership arrangement and hold a plurality ownership interest; the exact ArcLight percentage and legal investment vehicle are not publicly disclosed. Repsol completed a combined 20% sale to ArcLight and Centaurus in December 2023 and reported a retained 2.5% direct interest at year-end 2025. Public sources do not disclose a complete current capitalization table. The Leon and Castile fields, wells and leases and the subordinate Salamanca Infrastructure Finance, Salamanca FPS Infra and Salamanca OGL Infra entities are not separate PortCos. No ArcLight exit or signed pending Salamanca sale was identified through August 15, 2026.
company.headquarters: Keathley Canyon Block 689, U.S. Gulf of Mexico

milestones.event: Salamanca Infrastructure LLC was formed as a Delaware limited liability company.

LLOG announced the Salamanca development and an ownership and construction-financing arrangement with ArcLight-managed investment vehicles for the floating production system and associated export laterals.

Repsol completed the combined sale of a 20% Salamanca Infrastructure interest to ArcLight and Centaurus for $129 million and retained a 2.5% interest; the allocation between the purchasers was not disclosed.
The Salamanca floating production unit achieved first production from the Leon field, bringing the refurbished 60,000-barrel-per-day oil and 40-million-cubic-feet-per-day gas facility into operation.

company.name: Sequitur Renewables
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
company.description: Sequitur Renewables is an ArcLight-backed U.S. renewable-energy platform that owns and operates wind assets. ArcLight established the platform in 2022 around five operating PJM wind farms totaling 185 MW in Pennsylvania and West Virginia; public regulatory sources establish an October 2022 closing but conflict on the exact day. Sequitur expanded into California in May 2023 by acquiring an operating wind farm in Altamont Pass. ArcLight's current portfolio lists Sequitur as current, and ArcLight and GLEIF records attribute the company to ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P. Public sources do not disclose ArcLight's platform-level stake or immediate legal acquisition vehicle. No Sequitur-level exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: Sequitur Renewables, LLC was created as a Delaware limited liability company.
Sequitur Renewables entered into an agreement to acquire five operating PJM wind farms totaling 185 MW in Pennsylvania and West Virginia, establishing the operating platform.
ArcLight's Sequitur platform completed the acquisition of the five-project 185 MW PJM wind portfolio in October 2022; public sources differ by one day, so only month precision is recorded.
Sequitur acquired an operating wind farm in Altamont Pass, California, expanding beyond its original PJM portfolio.

company.name: Third Coast Infrastructure
company.description: Third Coast Infrastructure is a Houston-headquartered offshore and coastal midstream platform operating natural gas, crude oil and NGL gathering, transmission, processing and floating-production infrastructure across the U.S. Gulf Coast and Gulf of Mexico. The platform traces to American Midstream Partners, was taken private by ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V in 2019, added J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Infrastructure Investments Fund as a significant minority co-owner in 2021, and moved ArcLight's remaining 25.1% interest into ArcLight 3C SPV in July 2022. Current public materials list Third Coast CV as an ArcLight investment and identify a J.P. Morgan Asset Management-advised vehicle as an owner; exact current parent-platform ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. As of May 2026, company materials described approximately 1,900 pipeline miles, one gas processing plant and interests in four offshore floating production systems. No platform-level exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: American Midstream Partners, the predecessor to the current Third Coast platform, was formed in August 2009.
ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V affiliates completed the take-private of American Midstream Partners, which converted into Third Coast Midstream, LLC on the same date.

An Infrastructure Investments Fund affiliate made a significant minority investment in Third Coast Super Holdings, adding J.P. Morgan Asset Management's infrastructure strategy as a co-owner of the platform.

Third Coast completed the sale of an approximately 50% interest in subsidiary Lighthouse Super Holdings to a global infrastructure vehicle; the percentage does not establish the buyer's exact stake in the canonical parent platform.
ArcLight 3C SPV acquired ArcLight Fund V's remaining 25.1% interest in Third Coast Super Holdings, moving ArcLight's investment into a continuation vehicle.
Third Coast Super Holdings announced a $25 million loan upsize and repricing at the infrastructure subsidiary level.

Third Coast announced a $125 million term-loan upsize and described an active platform with approximately 1,900 pipeline miles, one gas processing plant and interests in four offshore floating production systems.

canonicalAfterImage.name: Third Coast Infrastructure
canonicalAfterImage.description: Third Coast Infrastructure is a Houston-headquartered offshore and coastal midstream platform operating natural gas, crude oil and NGL gathering, transmission, processing and floating-production infrastructure across the U.S. Gulf Coast and Gulf of Mexico. The platform traces to American Midstream Partners, was taken private by ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V in 2019, added J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Infrastructure Investments Fund as a significant minority co-owner in 2021, and moved ArcLight's remaining 25.1% interest into ArcLight 3C SPV in July 2022. Current public materials list Third Coast CV as an ArcLight investment and identify a J.P. Morgan Asset Management-advised vehicle as an owner; exact current parent-platform ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. As of May 2026, company materials described approximately 1,900 pipeline miles, one gas processing plant and interests in four offshore floating production systems. No platform-level exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

company.name: Thunderbird Renewables
company.description: Thunderbird Renewables is an ArcLight Infrastructure Partners Fund VIII portfolio of operating U.S. wind-generation assets managed through ArcLight's SkyVest Renewables platform. Regulatory filings show Fund VIII vehicles acquired a 50% indirect interest in the Lakefield Wind Project on February 21, 2025 and a 100% indirect interest in the Shiloh IV Wind Project on March 12, 2025, then acquired the remaining 50% Lakefield interest on July 1, 2025. ArcLight's 2025 ESG report presents Thunderbird as a 309 MW operating renewables portfolio. Thunderbird is counted as the manager-level portfolio, while SkyVest is the management platform and Lakefield and Shiloh IV are underlying assets. ArcLight's live investments page lists Thunderbird as Current. Public sources reviewed do not disclose Thunderbird's legal suffix, separate website, founding year, headquarters or manager-level ownership percentage, and no Thunderbird-level exit or signed pending transaction was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: ArcLight Fund VIII's F8 Renewables vehicle acquired a 50% indirect interest in the 205.5 MW Lakefield wind facility on February 21 and a 100% indirect interest in the 102.5 MW Shiloh IV wind facility on March 12, establishing Thunderbird's initial 2025 operating portfolio.
ArcLight Fund VIII's F8 Renewables vehicle acquired TAQA's remaining 50% indirect interest in the Lakefield wind facility, taking its project-level interest to 100%.

company.name: Zeem Solutions
company.ownershipVehicle: ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
company.description: Zeem Solutions, Inc. designs, owns and operates commercial electric-vehicle charging infrastructure and provides fleet-management and EV-asset services for commercial fleets. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Los Angeles, the company operates shared charging depots in Inglewood and Long Beach, California, and SeaTac, Washington, while also deploying charging at customer sites. ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII committed $50 million in 2022, and ArcLight continues to list Zeem as a current transformative-infrastructure investment. Public sources do not disclose ArcLight's ownership percentage, security class, immediate holding vehicle or exact legal closing date. LAZ Parking Realty Investors was announced as a prospective strategic and equity partner in 2022, but no legal closing or current direct ownership evidence was identified; no Zeem-level sale or signed pending exit was found through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: Zeem Solutions was founded to provide commercial electric-vehicle fleet infrastructure and services.
Zeem reported that its LAX charging depot had surpassed 350,000 charging sessions and delivered more than 13.4 million kWh of energy.

Zeem announced a $50 million capital commitment from a fund managed by ArcLight Capital Partners; ArcLight's portfolio reporting attributes Zeem to Fund VII, while the exact legal closing date and security class were not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Skyline Renewables
company.ownershipVehicle: Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund IV (AAIF IV)
company.description: Skyline Renewables is an Ardian-backed portfolio of operating and development-stage wind and solar generation assets in the United States. Ardian and Transatlantic Power Holdings created Skyline in 2018, and Ardian identifies it as an Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund IV investment. Ardian's 2025 integrated report continues to include Skyline in its infrastructure portfolio, while Skyline's current public page says it is managed by Dauntless Energy from Arlington, Virginia. Dauntless is a separate management company formed in 2024 to manage Skyline and 1370 Clean Energy; it is not a legal rename of Skyline, and 1370 is not consolidated into this record. Individual generation projects remain assets beneath Skyline. Ardian reported more than 1,050 MW of controlled wind and solar capacity in 2020, while Dauntless's current profile describes approximately 1 GW of Skyline managed assets. Public sources do not disclose Ardian's exact Skyline stake, security class, immediate holding vehicle or exact platform-equity closing day, and no Skyline-level exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: Ardian and Transatlantic Power Holdings created Skyline Renewables as a United States renewables platform, and Skyline completed its first acquisition, the 60 MW Whirlwind wind farm in Texas.
Ardian announced the final close of Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund IV and identified Skyline Renewables as one of the fund's first two investments.
Skyline announced the 250 MW Galloway solar project in Texas, taking its Ardian-backed controlled wind and solar portfolio to more than 1,050 MW.
Dauntless Energy was formed as a separate company to provide management services to the Skyline Renewables and 1370 Clean Energy portfolios; Skyline remained the Ardian investment identity.

company.name: Hill Top Energy Center
company.ownershipVehicle: Blackstone Energy Transition Partners IV AIV L.P., BXE IV (LUX) AIV SCSp and affiliated vehicles
company.description: Hill Top Energy Center is a 620 MW natural-gas combined-cycle power plant in Carmichaels, Pennsylvania that sells energy and capacity into PJM. Ardian Americas Infrastructure Funds acquired a 41.9% co-control interest in July 2019 while the plant was under construction, and the facility entered commercial operation in July 2021. Ardian acquired the remaining interest in April 2025. Blackstone announced a definitive agreement to acquire Hill Top on September 15, 2025, and a direct FERC consummation notice establishes that the transaction closed on March 26, 2026. Hill Top is now indirectly wholly owned through affiliated Blackstone funds, including Blackstone Energy Transition Partners IV AIV L.P. and BXE IV (LUX) AIV SCSp. The FERC record identifies 76.28% and 14.72% aggregator interests for those two vehicles; the internal allocation of the remaining 9% among other affiliated vehicles is not publicly disclosed. The plant company is the canonical PortCo, while buyer and seller holding entities are not counted separately. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

company.name: DSD Renewables
company.subsector: Distributed solar, storage, and EV charging
company.description: DSD Renewables, legally Distributed Solar Development, LLC, is a Schenectady-based U.S. distributed-energy platform that develops, finances, acquires, owns and operates commercial, industrial, municipal and community solar, storage and EV-charging infrastructure. The business began as GE Solar in 2012 and became the standalone DSD platform in 2019 with backing from BlackRock's Global Renewable Power II strategy. BlackRock acquired GE Renewable Energy's remaining interest in November 2020. Ares Management invested $200 million through its Infrastructure and Power strategy in March 2022 and became majority owner after a 2025 change-of-control and common-equity conversion. Cox Enterprises made a $250 million minority strategic investment in November 2023. July 2025 DSD materials identify Ares, BlackRock and Cox as current platform backers; exact current percentages are not publicly disclosed. DSD reported $238 million of financing for 188 operating distributed-generation projects totaling 233 MW in August 2025. Individual projects, project SPVs, financing counterparties and the BlackRock/GIP manager combination are outside the canonical PortCo boundary. No signed or completed DSD platform sale was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: GE launched the distributed-solar business later known as DSD Renewables as GE Solar.
BlackRock's Global Renewable Power II strategy acquired 80% of GE Solar in July 2019 as the business became DSD Renewables, then acquired GE Renewable Energy's remaining 20% on November 10, 2020.

Ares Management's Infrastructure and Power strategy invested $200 million of preferred equity on March 3, 2022; after a consensual 2025 change-of-control and common-equity conversion, Ares became majority owner in May 2025.
Cox Enterprises made a $250 million minority strategic investment in DSD Renewables.

The business began as GE Solar in 2012 and became the standalone DSD platform in 2019 with backing from BlackRock's Global Renewable Power II strategy. BlackRock acquired GE Renewable Energy's remaining interest in November 2020. Ares Management invested $200 million through its Infrastructure and Power strategy in March 2022 and became majority owner after a 2025 change-of-control and common-equity conversion. Cox Enterprises made a $250 million minority strategic investment in November 2023. July 2025 DSD materials identify Ares, BlackRock and Cox as current platform backers; exact current percentages are not publicly disclosed. DSD reported $238 million of financing for 188 operating distributed-generation projects totaling 233 MW in August 2025. Individual projects, project SPVs, financing counterparties and the BlackRock/GIP manager combination are outside the canonical PortCo boundary. No signed or completed DSD platform sale was identified through August 15, 2026.

company.name: Rover Pipeline
company.description: Rover Pipeline LLC is a large-scale interstate natural gas transmission system connecting Marcellus and Utica production in Pennsylvania and West Virginia with demand markets across Ohio, Michigan and the broader Midwest. The approximately 700-to-713-mile system has 3.425 Bcf/d of transportation capacity, is substantially contracted under long-term agreements and is operated by an Energy Transfer affiliate. The canonical PortCo is Rover Pipeline LLC; ET Rover Pipeline LLC, BCP Renaissance entities and Traverse Midstream Partners are ownership vehicles, while pipeline segments, interconnects and the separately owned Ohio River System are outside the Rover company boundary. Ares Management owns a 32.4% indirect interest through Ares Core Infrastructure Fund and the BCP Renaissance vehicles, Energy Transfer reports a 32.6% economic interest through ET Rover Pipeline LLC, and ePointZero owns 35% through Traverse. Blackstone's 32.44% indirect interest was realized when Ares acquired its vehicles on April 28, 2026. Rover's separately attributable headquarters, founding year and Energy Transfer's precise initial investment date are not publicly disclosed. No later Rover-level sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: ePointZero closed its $2.25 billion acquisition of Traverse Midstream Partners, including Traverse's 35% non-operated interest in Rover Pipeline.

Energy Transfer signed and announced an agreement for Blackstone's BCP Renaissance vehicle to acquire 49.9% of ET Rover Pipeline LLC, equivalent to an effective 32.44% indirect interest in Rover Pipeline.

Energy Transfer closed Blackstone's 49.9% acquisition of ET Rover Pipeline LLC, establishing Blackstone's 32.44% indirect Rover interest while Energy Transfer retained an effective 32.6% interest and Traverse retained 35%.
Rover completed construction and entered full commercial service as a major Appalachian Basin natural-gas takeaway pipeline.
Ares Core Infrastructure Fund acquired Blackstone's BCP Renaissance vehicles on April 28, taking a 32.4% indirect Rover interest; Ares and Blackstone announced the completed transaction on April 29.
