company.subsector: Fleet management and transportation staffing services
company.description: FleetLogix, Inc. is a San Diego-based provider of managed labor, fleet services and transportation staffing for rental-car operators and other mobility customers. LAZ Parking acquired a majority interest in FleetLogix in 2025, while Striker Partners and FleetLogix management reinvested. FleetLogix continues to operate under the FleetLogix Powered by LAZ brand. LAZ reported approximately 50 FleetLogix locations, including 37 airports in more than 20 states, and about 2,400 employees at acquisition. Argo Infrastructure Partners' directly evidenced manager-level investment is LAZ; FleetLogix is an active operating-company acquisition beneath that platform and is therefore archived from the standalone manager-level PortCo census. Public sources do not disclose the exact LAZ stake, FleetLogix closing date, Argo indirect percentage, fund vehicle, or founding year, and no later FleetLogix sale, legal merger, Argo exit or signed pending transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

company.name: Freight Ninja
company.subsector: Truck parking and industrial outdoor storage
company.description: Freight Ninja LLC is a Lombard, Illinois-based provider of industrial outdoor storage and managed parking for trucks, trailers, containers and commercial fleets. Established in 2022, the company provides site management, security, technology, access and operating support across a nationwide location network. LAZ Parking stated on May 6, 2025 that it had acquired a majority interest in Freight Ninja; the exact stake, retained seller or management ownership and legal closing date were not publicly disclosed. Freight Ninja's current site reports more than 65 facilities in 14 states, compared with 50 leased or managed locations, more than 300 acres and 10,000 spaces disclosed by LAZ at acquisition. Freight Ninja continues as a distinct active LLC, while Argo Infrastructure Partners' directly evidenced manager-level investment is LAZ. Freight Ninja is therefore archived from the standalone manager-level PortCo census as an acquisition beneath LAZ, with no legal merge, Argo exit or signed pending transaction identified through August 16, 2026.

LAZ Parking disclosed that it had acquired a majority interest in Freight Ninja; founder and CEO John Borsellino continued leading the distinct operating company.

company.name: INDIGO Park Canada Inc.
company.subsector: Parking management and urban mobility services
company.ownershipVehicle: Legacy direct attribution; actual exposure is indirect through LAZ Parking
company.description: INDIGO Park Canada Inc. is a Montreal-based parking, mobility and EV-services operator active across Canada. Founded in Quebec City in 1988, the company remained a distinct legal and operating business after LAZ Parking completed a 60% acquisition on June 30, 2025; INDIGO Group retained 40%. INDIGO Group's FY2025 accounts state that LAZ committed under the sale agreement to acquire the remaining 40% in 2029, but the exact future closing date and valuation are not yet publicly fixed. The current company site reports more than 340,000 parking stalls across 95 cities and nearly 450,000 active app users. Argo Infrastructure Partners' directly evidenced manager-level investment is LAZ, not INDIGO Park Canada. INDIGO Park Canada is therefore archived from the standalone manager-level PortCo census as an active LAZ subsidiary, without a legal merge, redirect or Argo exit; the contractual 2029 ownership change remains pending.

milestones.event: INDIGO Park Canada was founded in Quebec City and later established its headquarters in Montreal.
LAZ Parking completed the acquisition of 60% of INDIGO Park Canada; INDIGO Group retained the remaining 40%.
LAZ and INDIGO Group publicly announced the completed 60/40 partnership, with INDIGO Park Canada retaining its separate identity and John Laires remaining CEO.
INDIGO Group's FY2025 accounts confirmed its retained 40% interest and disclosed LAZ's contractual commitment to acquire that remaining stake in 2029.

company.name: Oneta Energy Center
company.description: Oneta Energy Center is a natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant in Broken Arrow, Wagoner County, Oklahoma, operated by Oneta Power, LLC. The single-plant business sells electricity and capacity into wholesale markets in the Southwest Power Pool. Its official site describes approximately 1,150 MW of nominal capacity, LS Power's 2019 sale announcement described 1,127 MW, and a FERC asset appendix attributes 1,086 MW for market-based-rate reporting. LS Power announced an agreement to sell Oneta and Carville to an Argo-managed investment vehicle on August 15, 2019; FERC reports a November 21, 2019 control-transfer date. EPA's 2023 facility record identifies Argo Infrastructure Partners LP as the 100% parent. Oneta Power and Oneta Energy Center are the operator and facility identities for one Argo investment, not separate manager-level portfolio companies. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026.

company.name: Pearl/Ruby Solar Portfolio
company.description: Pearl/Ruby Solar Portfolio is a 114 MW portfolio of contracted commercial and industrial distributed-solar assets comprising 134 operating sites across 12 U.S. states. The projects entered service between 2015 and 2018 and sell power under long-term PPAs to commercial, industrial and institutional hosts. Onyx Renewable Partners constructed and financed the assets, sold its sponsor-equity interest to funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners in a transaction publicly reported on February 5, 2019, and continued managing the projects. A June 2021 SEC filing lists Pearl/Ruby among Argo's holdings and separately lists Astro Solar. The current GRESB participant page includes Pearl\ Ruby as a non-listed Americas solar-PV asset, and Argo's July 2026 C&I solar release describes an active expanded platform. No later Pearl/Ruby-level sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026. company.description: Corning Energy Corporation is the parent platform for regulated natural gas and electric distribution utilities in New York and Pennsylvania, including Corning Natural Gas Corporation, Pike County Light & Power Company and Leatherstocking Gas Company. Pike is an operating subsidiary rather than a separate manager-level infrastructure investment. Corning's operating history dates to 1904, its holding company was formed in 2013, and it acquired all of Pike's stock from Orange & Rockland on August 31, 2016. Argo Infrastructure Partners completed the acquisition of 100% of the Corning parent platform on July 6, 2022 through the ACP Crotona ownership chain. A 2025 application proposed replacing the Argo general partner with an Apollo-controlled general partner, but the transaction did not close and was terminated in January 2026. Argo therefore remains the current owner, and no signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

Argo Infrastructure Partners completed the acquisition of 100% of Corning's common and preferred stock through the ACP Crotona ownership chain.
The Pennsylvania PUC held a hearing on an application for an indirect change of control of Corning Energy and its Pike and Leatherstocking subsidiaries involving Apollo and Argo-affiliated entities.

company.name: Black Hills Colorado IPP, LLC
company.ownershipVehicle: AIA Energy North America LLC / AIA Colchis LLC
company.description: Black Hills Colorado IPP, LLC is the manager-level independent-power investment within the broader Pueblo Airport Generating Station in Pueblo County, Colorado. The full site totals 440 MW, but the IPP company owns the 200 MW combined-cycle facility that entered service in 2012; the other 240 MW is utility-owned and is not part of Argo's investment. Black Hills Electric Generation retains a 50.1% controlling interest and the operating role, while Argo Infrastructure Partners manages the AIA Energy North America structure whose AIA Colchis vehicle holds the remaining 49.9%. AIA signed for the interest on February 12, 2016 and closed on April 14, 2016. The IPP sells capacity and energy to Black Hills Colorado Electric under a contract running through December 31, 2031. Black Hills' August 2026 filing continued to report the IPP noncontrolling interest, and no Argo/AIA exit or signed pending IPP ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026.

Black Hills signed a definitive agreement to sell a 49.9% member interest in Black Hills Colorado IPP for $215 million to Argo-managed AIA Energy North America LLC.
AIA Energy North America completed the 49.9% acquisition; Black Hills retained its 50.1% controlling interest and continued to operate the IPP facility.

Black Hills' second-quarter filing continued to report distributions to the Black Hills Colorado IPP noncontrolling interest; its separate NorthWestern parent merger remained pending and no IPP-level ownership transfer was reported.
Black Hills discloses that the agreement under which the 200 MW IPP provides capacity and energy to Black Hills Colorado Electric runs through December 31, 2031.

company.name: Smoky Mountain Holdings LLC
company.description: Smoky Mountain Holdings LLC is the manager-level joint venture owning four operating hydroelectric facilities in eastern Tennessee and western North Carolina: Cheoah, Calderwood, Chilhowee and Santeetlah. The portfolio totals 377 MW and has produced approximately 1.4 million MWh in an average year. Brookfield acquired the former Alcoa Tapoco assets in 2012. Argo Infrastructure Partners affiliate AMF Kimble Holdings acquired 50% in March 2023, while Brookfield affiliates and institutional partners retained the other 50%. company.name: UGI Utilities – Electric Division
company.description: UGI Utilities – Electric Division is a regulated electric transmission, distribution and retail utility serving more than 63,000 customers in Luzerne and Wyoming counties in northeastern Pennsylvania. The business operates approximately 2,700 miles of transmission and distribution lines and 14 substations. UGI Utilities, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of UGI Corporation, remains the current legal owner. Funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners LP signed an approximately $470 million definitive purchase agreement on April 28, 2026, but UGI's August 2026 Form 10-Q continued to classify the business as held for sale and expected closing in UGI fiscal Q2 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and applicable regulatory approvals. The exact Argo fund, manager-level stake, standalone legal suffix, headquarters, founding year and separate website are not publicly disclosed. Wyoming Valley Electric Holdings LLC and related acquisition entities are transaction vehicles for this same target, not separate PortCos. No legal close, termination, resale or revised timetable was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: UGI Utilities announced a definitive agreement to sell its Pennsylvania Electric Division to funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners LP for approximately $470 million, subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
UGI Utilities, Inc. and Wyoming Valley Electric Holdings LLC filed their joint Federal Power Act section 203 application in FERC docket EC26-118-000.
UGI's fiscal 2026 third-quarter Form 10-Q continued to classify the electric utility as held for sale and expected closing in UGI fiscal Q2 2027, confirming the Argo acquisition remained pending.

company.name: US Water Systems
company.description: US Water Systems is an unsupported repository umbrella for two separate municipal water and wastewater concession investments: the Bayonne water and wastewater concession in New Jersey and Middletown Water Joint Venture LLC in Pennsylvania. SUEZ and New York regulatory materials describe the concessions separately, and Water Capital Partners' current project list does the same; no reviewed source identifies a legal US Water Systems entity or one operating platform above both investments. Argo acquired KKR and SUEZ interests in the two concession SPVs in 2017, while Veolia/SUEZ remained the operator and minority participant. Current municipal, operator and project records show both concessions remain active. Apollo's announced acquisition of the Argo manager did not close and was terminated in January 2026, so Apollo never became an owner of the assets. This umbrella record is archived from the manager-level PortCo census without a redirect to prevent double counting; the separate Bayonne and Middletown records remain published. No later sale, concession termination, signed pending exit or ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: Bayonne entered a 40-year water and wastewater concession with a KKR and United Water consortium; the concession is a separate canonical investment rather than part of a legal US Water Systems platform.
Middletown Borough executed its separate long-term water and wastewater concession agreement with Middletown Water Joint Venture LLC.
KKR and SUEZ transferred their respective interests in the separate Bayonne and Middletown concession SPVs to Argo Infrastructure Partners; SUEZ retained minority operating interests.
Middletown Borough's operating report documented continued active water and wastewater system operations under the separate Middletown concession.

A New York regulatory filing confirmed that Apollo's proposed acquisition of the Argo manager had not closed and that the agreement and transaction were terminated, creating no concession-level ownership change.

company.name: Waihonu Solar Farm
company.description: Waihonu Solar Farm is the collective name for Waihonu North Solar, a 5.0 MW photovoltaic plant, and Waihonu South Solar, a 1.5 MW photovoltaic plant, in Mililani on Oʻahu. The operating projects comprise 26,232 modules on approximately 12 acres and sell electricity to Hawaiian Electric under a power purchase agreement. Argo Infrastructure Partners acquired Waihonu as an underlying asset in its July 21, 2022 purchase of Hawaiʻi Gas and related businesses. Hawaiʻi Gas states that a solar energy provider acquired Waihonu in 2025, and the 2025 early-release Form EIA-860 data reports ERCAM LLC as the utility and operator for both plants. The projects remain operational, but no reviewed source establishes ERCAM as an infrastructure-fund manager. Waihonu is therefore realized and archived from the manager-level PortCo census without a redirect; Hawaiʻi Gas remains a distinct published platform. The exact 2025 closing date, transaction value and ERCAM parent are not publicly disclosed, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

Argo Infrastructure Partners completed its acquisition of Hawaiʻi Gas and related smaller energy businesses, including the Waihonu solar projects.

Hawaiʻi Gas reported that a solar energy provider acquired Waihonu; Form EIA-860 subsequently reported ERCAM LLC as the utility and operator for both plants. The exact closing date and transaction value were not publicly disclosed.
